stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a method to scale visuomotor context for robot policies up to 8K timesteps.
Achieves this massive context scaling without increasing inference latency, a significant technical hurdle.
Enables new capabilities like one-shot in-context imitation and on-the-fly policy improvement in robots.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The research demonstrates that large language models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining.
These poisoning attacks can introduce harmful behaviors that are difficult to detect and mitigate.
The study expands the scope of poisoning attacks beyond limited datasets to cover large-scale, heterogeneous pretraining corpora.

stories.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
stories.author: Linxi "Jim" Fan
bullet_points: Introduces RoboTTT, a new framework for robot policies that scales visuomotor context significantly.
Achieves context lengths up to 8K timesteps, a three-order-of-magnitude improvement over current state-of-the-art.
Enables advanced capabilities like one-shot in-context imitation and on-the-fly policy improvement without increasing inference latency.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million from prominent investors.
The company boasts a substantial developer base, currently serving 8.9 million developers.
The news highlights the growing commercial and adoption momentum behind open-source LLM serving tools.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved when running on Apple Silicon via Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedups reach up to 90% when utilizing coding agents, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes a 'local-first' approach, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads for Apple devices.
The feature is currently available in preview, signaling a push for local, high-speed AI inference on Macs.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core feature emphasizes running AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy.

stories.title: Google-backed satellites for wildfire detection launch as smoke chokes US, Canada
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Google-backed FireSat program is deploying satellites specifically for wildfire detection.
The new system is designed to identify wildfires that existing satellite technology often misses.
The deployment is timely, addressing severe smoke issues currently affecting the US and Canada.

stories.title: San Francisco orders Apple, Google to remove nudify apps from app stores
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: San Francisco has mandated that Apple and Google remove 'nudify' applications from their respective app stores.
The regulatory action targets apps that employ manipulative design patterns, potentially impacting user experience and data ethics.
The ruling suggests significant financial implications for Google and Apple, who are estimated to have earned millions from these apps.

stories.title: SceneBind: Binding What and Where Across Vision, Audio and Language
stories.author: Eli Shlizerman
bullet_points: SceneBind introduces an omni-modal representation capable of jointly understanding vision, audio, and language in realistic scenes.
It specifically addresses a limitation in existing encoders by integrating explicit 3D spatial structure alongside instance-level semantics.
The core innovation involves representing scenes as semantic-spatial entities using a global embedding and object-centric slots.

stories.title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
stories.author: Stefan Feuerriegel
bullet_points: Introduces AutoSynthesis, an end-to-end multi-agent system designed for automated meta-analysis.
Addresses the current bottleneck of manual and difficult-to-scale quantitative evidence synthesis in various fields.
The system automates the entire process from natural language research question formulation to literature screening and data extraction.

stories.title: When Words Are Safe But Actions Kill: Probing Physical Danger Beyond Text Safety in Hidden-State Risk Space
stories.author: Ke Xu
bullet_points: Investigates the gap between text-level safety and physical safety when LLMs control embodied agents.
Demonstrates that linguistically safe instructions can lead to dangerous actions when grounded in the real world.
Uses hidden-state analysis to show that 'content danger' and 'physical danger' are separable signals within LLM representations.

stories.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
stories.author: Kyle Lo
bullet_points: The paper demonstrates that Large Language Models (LLMs) can be poisoned during pretraining using computational propaganda.
Previous research on data poisoning was limited, often focusing on small, established datasets like Wikipedia.
The study highlights the risk of poisoning attacks interacting with complex data curation pipelines, leading to hard-to-detect harmful behaviors in LLMs.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now available via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Dave Eggers told OpenAI staff  that ChatGPT was ‘silencing an entire generation’
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Author Dave Eggers voiced concerns to OpenAI staff that ChatGPT is 'silencing an entire generation.'
The discussion took place during a talk given by Eggers to approximately 200 OpenAI employees.
The story highlights the growing cultural and creative concerns surrounding the impact of large language models on writers.

stories.title: Will AI fix prior authorization—or make it worse?
stories.author: Joshua Cohen, Undark Magazine
bullet_points: Government is piloting an AI program to automate insurance coverage decisions.
The article explores the potential dual impact of AI on prior authorization processes.
The core question is whether AI will streamline or complicate existing healthcare administrative hurdles.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual and time-consuming process of editing scientific diagrams during paper revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex, heterogeneous visual grammar of scientific infographics (schematics, plots, etc.).

stories.title: Beyond Success Rate: Cost-Aware Evaluation of Offensive and Defensive Security Agents
stories.author: Yaron Singer
bullet_points: The paper proposes a new evaluation metric for AI security agents that incorporates computational cost alongside success rate.
Current security agent evaluations often overlook the operational cost (inference budget) of reasoning steps and tool calls.
The research tests this cost-aware evaluation on offensive (Cybench) and defensive (Splunk BOTS v1) security tasks.

stories.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: Introduces SearchOS, a system-level multi-agent framework designed to improve information-seeking capabilities.
Addresses a key limitation in current LLM agents: getting trapped in repetitive search loops when initial queries fail.
Focuses on enhancing the robustness and completeness of open-domain information retrieval by managing interaction history.

stories.title: teLLMe Why (Ain't Nothing but a Jam): Exploratory Causal Analysis of Urban Driving Data
stories.author: Jorge Ortiz
bullet_points: Introduces 'teLLMe,' a system designed for exploratory causal analysis of urban driving datasets.
Addresses the challenge of answering causal questions (e.g., 'How would rain change traffic density?') using purely observational traffic data.
Combines causal structure learning with data derived from structured event tables built from dashcam annotations.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training priorities, leading to suboptimal performance for later-added languages.
Adding new languages can cause increased tokenization overhead (more tokens per word), negatively impacting latency, compute, and energy.
The issue is exacerbated in compact models where the embedding and LM-head matrices are a larger fraction of the total parameters compared to large cloud models.

stories.title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Xuan Luo
bullet_points: Addresses the real-time constraint challenge in dynamic novel view synthesis from streaming video.
Identifies the computational bottleneck of traditional Test-Time Training (TTT) due to required gradient-based memory updates.
Proposes a novel 'Online Neural Space Time Memory' to balance long-horizon memory with real-time performance.

stories.title: Mutable Low-Rank Sketches for Retrain-Free Recommendation
stories.author: Nick Clayton
bullet_points: Addresses the 'embedding staleness' bottleneck in two-stage recommendation systems.
Introduces 'mutable sketches' using a KP-tree to store user preferences sparsely.
Allows for on-the-fly embedding updates as new ratings arrive, improving prediction accuracy.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on initial pre-training corpus priorities.
Adding new languages later can lead to inefficient tokenization (more tokens per word), increasing latency and resource use.
The issue is exacerbated in compact models where embedding/LM-head matrices are a larger fraction of total parameters.

stories.title: NeuronSoup: Evolving Asynchronous, Shared-Neuron Temporal Graphs without Backpropagation
stories.author: Subodh Kalia
bullet_points: Introduces NeuronSoup, a novel neural computation architecture moving away from traditional synchronous, layer-by-layer processing.
Features asynchronous, delay-mediated signal propagation through a pool of physically shared neurons.
Proposes a mechanism for continuous-valued signal routing through variable-length paths without relying on backpropagation.

stories.title: BadWAM: When World-Action Models Dream Right but Act Wrong
stories.author: Xinchao Wang
bullet_points: World-Action Models (WAMs) are a new approach in embodied control that links action generation with future world prediction.
The paper introduces 'BadWAM' to challenge the assumption that this coupling inherently leads to robust and safe robotic behavior.
BadWAM provides a unified framework for modeling and evaluating the potential failures in these advanced control models.

stories.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
stories.author: Jürgen Schmidhuber
bullet_points: SciDiagramEdit addresses the manual, time-consuming process of editing scientific figures during paper revisions.
The system aims to automate figure editing using natural language instructions.
The challenge lies in the complex, heterogeneous visual grammar of scientific diagrams (schematics, plots, arrows, etc.).

stories.title: Bridge Evidence: Static Retrieval Utility Does Not Predict Causal Utility in Multi-Step Agentic Search
stories.author: Shubham Chatterjee
bullet_points: Traditional retrieval evaluation (static usefulness) fails when LLMs act as multi-step search agents.
The utility of a document in agentic search depends on what it enables the agent to do next, not just its immediate answer quality.
The research highlights a critical gap between static document relevance and dynamic, multi-turn reasoning capabilities in AI agents.

stories.title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Design Lessons for Trustworthy Multimodal VQA
stories.author: Steven A. Hicks
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need for trustworthy and interpretable multimodal AI in healthcare, specifically for Visual Question Answering (VQA).
The study analyzes nine systems using GI endoscopy data to compare performance, noting that strong challenge performance doesn't guarantee faithful clinical reasoning.
It highlights the limitations of parameter-efficient adaptation methods when translating technical gains into reliable clinical explanations.

stories.title: TikStance: A Multimodal and Hierarchical Dataset for Multi-target Stance Analysis in TikTok Political Conversations
stories.author: Bowen Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces TikStance, a new multimodal and hierarchical dataset specifically for stance analysis.
Addresses the gap in computational analysis for political discourse on short-video platforms like TikTok.
The dataset is designed for political stance detection, covering discussions around major figures in the 2024 U.S. election.

stories.title: In-Place Tokenizer Expansion for Pre-trained LLMs
stories.author: Mathias Lechner
bullet_points: Current LLM tokenizers are fixed based on pre-training corpus priorities, leading to suboptimal performance for later-added languages.
Adding new languages can cause increased tokenization overhead (more tokens per word), negatively impacting latency and resource usage.
The issue is exacerbated in compact models where embedding/LM-head matrices are a larger fraction of total parameters compared to large cloud models.

stories.title: Mask-Aware Policy Gradients for Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Philipp Krähenbühl
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs).
Current methods struggle with log-likelihood estimation in MDLMs by only modeling token predictions, ignoring generation order.
The research proposes a 'Mask-Aware Policy Gradient' approach to account for the two decisions made at each generation step.

stories.title: Optimizing RAG at Scale: Chunking, Retrieval, and the Bayesian Search That Cut Latency 40%
stories.author: imus_d7584cbc8ee9b0336256
bullet_points: Focuses on optimizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems for large-scale deployment.
Addresses key technical challenges in RAG, specifically chunking and retrieval mechanisms.
Introduces a Bayesian Search technique that reportedly achieved a 40% reduction in latency.

stories.title: Optimizing RAG at Scale: Chunking, Retrieval, and the Bayesian Search That Cut Latency 40%
